brief.headline: Close the ₹28.69 L gap to our best prices and move to 30-day payment to free ₹16.02 L working capital — we are 47.43% of their revenue and they cannot afford to lose us.

priceAsk.summary: Demand price parity with Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic across all rigid plastic packaging SKUs to eliminate the ₹28.69 L annual excess.
priceAsk.target: ₹0.81/NOS for PP CAP PLAS 28MM INDUCTUCTION WAD (currently ₹1.08/NOS), ₹1.38/NOS for HDPE BOT WHITE 30ML WITH RING MARK (currently ₹1.53/NOS), and ₹0.35/NOS for MESU. CUP 30MM TRANS.PP 2.5/5/10ML (currently ₹0.46/NOS)
priceAsk.basis: We already pay these lower prices to Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic for identical items — the 33.2% gap on caps, 10.7% gap on bottles, and 30.6% gap on measuring cups is not justified and costs us ₹28.69 L annually.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 Days After Receipt to 30 Days After Receipt to match industry practice and free working capital for both parties.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹16.02 L one-time working capital release for FDC; they already stretch their own suppliers to 39d vs 23d peer median, so this is entirely fair.

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp is small (₹4.11 Cr revenue) and weak: their 6.0% net margin is less than half the 15.0% peer median, and they carry debt at 1.13x debt-to-equity. Our ₹1.95 Cr annual spend represents 47.43% of their total revenue — losing us would cripple them. Their 11.5% return on capital trails the 15.3% peer median. They are rated C (51/100) health and flagged as a small entity requiring verification. However, their tight margin means aggressive price cuts will hurt them badly, so we should balance price with payment-term and volume commitments. Their 4.77x interest coverage shows they can service debt, but cash matters — offer faster payment only in exchange for deeper discounts.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹28.69 L per year versus the best prices we already secure from other suppliers
On our largest SKU, PP CAP PLAS 28MM INDUCTUCTION WAD, Cincorp charges ₹1.08/NOS while Mars Plastics supplies at ₹0.81/NOS — a 33.2% gap costing us ₹14.05 L annually
FDC represents 47.43% of Cincorp's ₹4.11 Cr revenue, giving us decisive negotiating power
Cincorp's 6.0% net margin is far below the 15.0% peer median, signaling tight profitability and limited room to absorb our business loss
They stretch their own suppliers to 39d payables versus 23d peer median, so asking for 30-day terms is equitable
Moving to 30-day terms releases ₹16.02 L of working capital for FDC

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter supplying pharma bottles, caps, and preforms — top second-source candidate already identified for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma) with A health rating — strong, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Mars Plastics
alternates.why: Currently supplies us PP CAP PLAS 28MM INDUCTUCTION WAD at ₹0.81/NOS and HDPE BOT WHITE 30ML at ₹1.38/NOS — proven capability on our two largest SKUs.

risks: Cincorp is flagged as a small entity (<₹10 Cr) requiring verification — confirm production capacity and financial stability before committing large volumes.
Their below-peer 6.0% margin means aggressive price cuts could push them into losses or force them to walk away — balance price demands with volume certainty or payment-term sweeteners.
With 1.13x debt-to-equity and ₹1.95 Cr total debt, financial stress could disrupt supply continuity — monitor their liquidity and have Manjushree Technopack or Mold-Tek ready to step in.
We are 47.43% of their revenue, so if they lose us they may not survive — this gives us leverage but also means we need a transition plan if negotiations fail.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more than our best suppliers on identical items — let's work together to close that gap and move to 30-day terms so we can both improve our working capital.
